{
  "title": "The Weight of the Void",
  "hook_family": "observation",
  "hook": "Silence isn't the absence of sound. It is a presence.",
  "curiosity": "When someone stops speaking, the air between you changes. It thickens.",
  "psychological_mechanism": "The human mind is wired to seek patterns. When a familiar voice goes quiet, your brain begins to fill the vacuum. You start constructing narratives to bridge the gap. You look for meaning in the pause. You interpret a lack of motion as a deliberate choice.",
  "realization": "It feels loud because your imagination is doing the heavy lifting. You aren't hearing their silence; you are hearing your own fears echoing in the space they left behind.",
  "final_line": "Peace isn't found in the answer. It’s found in accepting the unknown.",
  "visual_metaphor": "A single chair remains in a room where a fire has burned out, the grey ash still warm."
}
